title: The Base Case of Frobenius/Zolotarev: sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/p) = (a/p)
description: Closes the loop the parent (CRT decomposition of the Zolotarev permutation) left open. The parent reduced the Jacobi-symbol generalization of Zolotarev's lemma to a single missing base case: sign(ringMulPerm a on the WHOLE field ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a. This entry proves it. The genuinely new content is a fixed-point sign-restriction bridge — multiplication by a unit fixes 0 and permutes the nonzero residues, so its sign on all of ℤ/p equals its sign on the units (ℤ/p)ˣ (via Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypePerm and the field equivalence unitsEquivNeZero). Composing the bridge with Zolotarev's lemma on the units gives the base case, and composing the base case with the parent's CRT multiplicativity gives the Jacobi value as a product of Legendre symbols for a two-prime squarefree odd modulus. The units-level Zolotarev lemma is re-established self-contained on the modern Mathlib API, since the grandparent file no longer compiles.

overview.text: Zolotarev's lemma naturally lives on the units (ℤ/p)ˣ, where the sign of multiplication-by-a equals the quadratic character. The Frobenius/Jacobi/CRT setting, by contrast, acts on all of ℤ/p. The bridge between the two is purely permutation-theoretic and uses no number theory: 0 is a fixed point, so the sign is carried entirely by the units. This single observation is the glue that lets the cyclic-character argument (prime case) and the CRT product argument (composite case) combine into one statement about Jacobi values.
overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev (1872) identified the Legendre symbol (a/p) with the sign of the permutation x ↦ ax on (ℤ/p)ˣ. Frobenius (1914) generalized this to composite moduli and the Jacobi symbol, with the Chinese Remainder Theorem as the mechanism. The grandparent entry (elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01) formalized only the prime/units case; its child (oq-01-oq-03) formalized the structural CRT decomposition on the whole ring ℤ/n but explicitly left open the base case sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a — 'the remaining glue' combining the units-level lemma with a fixed-point sign-restriction argument. This entry supplies that glue.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question (the listed next step of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03): prove the base case sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a for a prime p, combining the parent's units-level zolotarev_lemma with a fixed-point sign-restriction argument, then combine with CRT multiplicativity to reach Jacobi values.
overview.proofStrategy: 1. Fixed-point bridge (the new content): multiplication by a unit a keeps nonzero residues nonzero (a·x ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ 0) and fixes 0. By Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypePerm the sign of ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p equals the sign of its restriction to {x // x ≠ 0}; the field equivalence unitsEquivNeZero : (ℤ/p)ˣ ≃ {x // x ≠ 0} identifies that restriction with mulPerm a, and sign_eq_sign_of_equiv transports the sign — giving sign(ringMulPerm a) = sign(mulPerm a). 2. Units-level Zolotarev, re-established self-contained: both sign(mulPerm ·) and the quadratic character are multiplicative; on a generator g both equal -1 (mulPerm g is a single (p-1)-cycle, so its sign is -(-1)^(p-1) = -1 since p-1 is even; and a generator is a non-square via an orderOf_pow' argument). Since every unit is a power of g, the two characters agree everywhere. 3. Base case: chain the bridge, the units-level lemma, and the definitional bridge legendreSym = quadraticChar. 4. Loop closing: for distinct odd primes p, q the parent's sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd plus the base case express sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pq) as a product of two Legendre symbols — the two-factor Jacobi value.
keyInsights: The passage from the units (ℤ/p)ˣ to the whole field ℤ/p costs nothing in sign: 0 is a fixed point of multiplication-by-a, so sign_subtypePerm carries the entire sign onto the units.
In a field, (ℤ/p)ˣ ≃ {x : ℤ/p // x ≠ 0} (unitsEquivNeZero), and under this equivalence the nonzero-restriction of ringMulPerm a is exactly the units permutation mulPerm a.

Zolotarev's lemma on the units needs only two generator facts: a single (p-1)-cycle has sign -1 (p-1 even), and a generator of a cyclic group of even order is a non-square (orderOf u² = orderOf u / gcd(orderOf u, 2) < orderOf u).

The two-factor Jacobi value emerges by composing this base case with the parent's CRT multiplicativity — the base case anchors each CRT factor to a Legendre value while the CRT lemma supplies the product structure.
legendreSym p a is definitionally quadraticChar (ℤ/p) a, so the Legendre formulation follows from the quadratic-character formulation with only a val-cast round-trip.
prerequisites: Permutation sign and its behaviour under subtype restriction (Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypePerm, sign_eq_sign_of_equiv)
Cycle structure and sign of cycles (Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.sign)
The quadratic character and Legendre symbol (Mathlib LegendreSymbol API)
Cyclic structure and order arithmetic of (ℤ/p)ˣ (orderOf_pow', orderOf_eq_card_of_forall_mem_zpowers)

sections.title: Closing the loop — Jacobi values for a two-prime odd modulus
sections.summary: sign_ringMulPerm_eq_legendre_mul: for distinct odd primes p, q, sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pq) is the product of the Legendre symbols of the two CRT components, combining the base case with the parent's CRT multiplicativity.

meta.assumptions: None. The file has 0 axiom declarations, 0 sorries, no native_decide, and no assumption-carrying structures. All results are fully machine-checked against Mathlib v4.26.0 (#print axioms on the three headline theorems reports only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound). Self-contained note: the grandparent file ElementaryQuadraticReciprocityOQ01 (the units-level Zolotarev lemma) no longer compiles against Mathlib 4.26.0 (forward references and deprecations — a separate bit-rot repair), so the units-level statement is re-established from scratch here on the modern API, importing only the building parent ElementaryQuadraticReciprocityOQ01OQ03 for the CRT machinery. Honest scope: the base case is complete and unconditional for p ≠ 2. The loop-closing corollary is stated for a TWO-PRIME modulus p·q; fully general squarefree (and then prime-power) odd n follows by iterating sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd over the factorization, a routine induction adding no new idea, left to a follow-up.

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the base case the parent left open: sign(ringMulPerm a on the whole field ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a. The new content is a fixed-point sign-restriction bridge (sign on ℤ/p equals sign on the units, because 0 is a fixed point); the units-level Zolotarev lemma is re-established self-contained, and the base case combines with the parent's CRT multiplicativity to express the two-factor Jacobi value as a product of Legendre symbols on ℤ/pq.
conclusion.implications: Completes the conceptual loop of the Frobenius/Zolotarev generalization for the two-prime squarefree case: the multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol in its denominator (CRT shadow, parent) plus the prime base case (this entry) together identify the whole-ring permutation sign with the Jacobi value. The fixed-point bridge isolates exactly why the units-level character argument suffices for the whole-field/Frobenius setting.
openQuestions: Iterate sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd over the full prime factorization to obtain sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for all squarefree odd n (a routine induction over Nat.factorization).
Handle prime-power factors p^e (e ≥ 2), where (ℤ/p^e)ˣ has even order, to reach the full Frobenius statement for every odd n.
